correctness.rationale: Direct substitution into the full Newton update proves the multiplicative positive-energy identity and exact affine log recurrence. For subcritical exponent a two-sided stationary contraction coupling proves distributional convergence and a.s. recurrent extrema; Gaussian small-ball asymptotics give exact Mellin integrability cutoff. At the critical exponent strong law and iterated-logarithm law cover negative, positive and zero drift; expectation uses independent trace moments. Above criticality the exponentially rescaled log recurrence converges a.s. to a continuous full-support signed series. Strict concavity in positive Hessian eigenvalues proves spectral Schur monotonicity, and the polar Gaussian angular identity gives the exact two-dimensional formula and trace-4 counterdirection. The included deterministic reproducer passed 1927 supportive checks; finite checks do not substitute for proofs.

value.rationale: The newly motivated borderline of a 2026 noisy Newton rule exhibits a sharp structurally surprising distinction: Hessian spectral anisotropy can change almost-sure convergence to divergence while leaving the full expected objective trajectory untouched at fixed trace. For trace 4 the diagonal SPD Hessians (2,2) and (3.9,0.1) have opposite log drifts but the same expected growth 2^n, a checkable warning that ordinary expected-error guarantees can be nonrepresentative. Explicit two-dimensional threshold and across-exponent limiting behaviors offer practical mathematical benchmarks, while the result does not overclaim extension to nonquadratic objectives.
